transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-02
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 38 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Thompson, Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao (Aurora Health)

Summary:
Quick SDK integration walkthrough focusing on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, authentication options (API key vs SSO/SAML for enterprise), environment setup for local dev and CI, and next steps for a small POC to validate latency/cost. Security questions on KMS and data retention were raised; Redwood to share docs.

Topics:
- Quickstart flow: install, env vars, API key + optional SSO
- Python example: streaming vs non-streaming generation
- TypeScript/Node quickstart: async/await usage, retries
- Auth: API keys, SSO, service principals, KMS integration
- Env & CI: secrets in CI, sample dockerfile, terraform snippets referenced
- POC scope: throughput/latency targets and metrics to collect

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan, i'll run quick intro then pass to samir for the SDK deep dive. how's the audio by the way?
00:06 Maya (Aurora): good thanks, excited to see the SDK examples, we've been looking at the console but want to get devs up-and-running fast.
00:15 Samir (Redwood SE): awesome, i'll share my screen in a sec. high level, we'll go through python quickstart, ts/ node quickstart, auth patterns and then q&a. feel free to jump in.
00:29 (screen share starts)
00:35 Samir: okay opening the repo — link is in the chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: repo link pasted). first file is README, shows install: pip install redwood-sdk and npm install @redwood/inference.
00:48 Samir: python example, super minimal: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, then from redwood import Client, client = Client(), resp = client.generate("Summarize this medical note..."). importantly we show both streaming and non-streaming examples.
01:05 Maya: quick question — can we do SSO or do devs have to use API keys for the POC?
01:12 Jordan: for the hosted trial you can use API keys; for enterprise we support SSO/SAML and service principals for private deployments. we'll share the SAML integration doc.
01:25 Priya (Aurora - Security): and on keys — is there KMS integration so keys aren't stored in plaintext on our side? need to confirm SOC2 guidance.
01:35 Samir: yes on private deployments you can use customer-managed KMS or HSM, and we integrate with common cloud providers. i'll attach the KMS overview doc after.
01:45 Liam (Aurora SRE): for CI secrets what's the recommended pattern? put REDWOOD_API_KEY in vault, pass to container env?
01:52 Samir: yep recommended is vault/secret manager + short-lived tokens. our quickstart includes a sample dockerfile and a github actions snippet showing how to pull secrets.
02:05 Jordan: note that for Dedicated or Private we can provision service accounts with IP allowlists, etc, so CI machines can call the dedicated endpoint rather than public hosted API.
02:18 Samir: switching to TypeScript quickstart. code: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) — abort / timeout handling and retry examples are in utils/retries.ts.
02:36 Samir: small gotcha: older examples used X-API-KEY header; modern SDKs use bearer tokens and the client takes care of header formatting. sometimes transcripts have it as x-api-key in docs but code uses Authorization: Bearer token.
02:50 Maya: regarding streaming — if we use streaming for assistant UI, do we get token-level billing or is it aggregated?
02:58 Jordan: token level billing still applies but streaming doesn't change unit costs, it just impacts how you receive chunks. our console shows token breakdown per route.
03:10 Maya: good. also about model pinning — can we pin a verifier model or quantized variant for cost?
03:18 Samir: yes you can pin model versions in the request: model: "redwood-13b-q4" for example. for POC we can recommend a quantized variant to hit latency/cost targets.
03:30 (15s pause, typing noises)
03:47 Samir: now quick demo - run python quickstart locally. i'm switching to terminal.
04:02 Samir: step 1: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXXX (obviously use your test key). step 2: python -m venv venv && pip install -r requirements.txt. step 3: python examples/generate_note.py --stream.
04:20 Samir: you'll see streaming chunks: [00:04] "Patient presents with..." — note transcription mismatch sometimes shows patient names as similar sounding words, e g "Patterson" vs "Paterson" in transcribed output, but that's downstream model text not infra.
04:40 Liam: what's our expected latency for a 512-token reply on a dedciated instance? (sic)
04:47 Samir: on dedicated gpus for redwood-13b we typically see 150-250ms per token at 1-2 concurrent requests with batching. for batchy workloads we recommend using continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce cost. i'll run a baseline and share numbers.
05:10 Jordan: we should call that out in the POC targets — 200ms/token at 1ccr (concurrent client requests) as a baseline, adjust as needed.
05:22 Maya: ok that helps. on compliance — Priya, any specific ask from your side?
05:30 Priya: we need to confirm data residency options, retention, and audit logs. also whether Redwood stores KV cache or customer-only.
05:40 Samir: KV cache is per-tenant and can be disabled; for private deployments it's under your control. audit logs and exportable traces are available in the console. we'll share SOC2+ISO docs.
05:55 Jordan: i'm noting action items: share quickstart, perf run, security docs.
06:05 (noise)
06:20 Maya: can you also share a sample terraform snippet for provisioning the private agent? we want to estimate infra ops for private POC.
06:28 Samir: yes in infra/terraform/ there is an example for aws and gcp. it includes EKS node group, iam bindings, and the redwood agent helm chart. we'll add a comment about network policy and private s3 endpoints.
06:45 (short cross talk)
07:00 Samir: small demo of TypeScript code running — hitting the local dev server. shows average 80ms for first token due to cold start, subsequent tokens ~40ms. note: cold starts vary with model size and container warmness.
07:22 Liam: for the POC do we want to test hosted vs dedicated?
07:28 Jordan: recommend starting hosted for speed, then move to dedicated if you need sustained concurrency or data isolation. because you can route by policy we can failover to hosted if dedicated is saturated.
07:42 Priya: licensing — will there be a separate contract for private deployment or it's same as Dedicated?
07:48 Jordan: Private typically has a platform fee and support add-on; Dedicated is capacity commit. we'll loop in AE/sales for pricing details after this call.
07:58 (note: 07:58 marker, but call continues)
08:05 Maya: can you show how to enable structured output / function calling?
08:12 Samir: yep quick snippet: client.generate({ prompt, functions: [{name: 'extract_medical_entities', schema: {...}}], mode: 'function_call' }) — the SDK will return a structured JSON and we provide validation helpers. caveat: function calling has limits per model, check the docs.
08:35 Maya: perfect. any lint or code style blockers for TS team?
08:40 Samir: nothing special, the TS SDK is typed; we publish types and examples. the only thing is build targets if you're on older node versions, but we include a polyfill.
08:52 Jordan: circling back to auth — for the enterprise flow we support OIDC + SAML; for service-to-service we recommend short-lived tokens and rotating keys. Priya, would you prefer SAML or service principals for POC?
09:06 Priya: for POC, service principal with scoped keys and vault-managed secrets is fine. for prod we'll push the SAML/SSO route.
09:14 Jordan: got it. we'll provide a template for roles and IAM scoping.
09:20 (typing)
09:30 Maya: about billing — is there cost estimation per 1M tokens for the quantized models?
09:36 Jordan: yes we'll include a cost spreadsheet; in Optimize we have recommended profiles that map quantization + batch configs to $/1k tokens. i'll attach that.
09:48 Samir: another thing — model fallbacks: if the requested model isn't available in region, we can route to compatible variant; you'll see this in the console routing policy page.
10:02 Maya: ok good. any integration gotchas with observability? we use datadog — how do we pull metrics?
10:10 Samir: we have integrations and a tracing hook; our console emits metrics and you can forward via a prometheus exporter or datadog agent. examples in ops/observability.
10:25 Jordan: time check — about 25 minutes in. want to open for questions and confirm next steps.
25:40 Maya: quick question — does your SDK buffer retries automatically or do we need to wrap calls?
25:48 Samir: client has built-in retry/backoff and jitter, but you can override. we also provide an example retry policy tuned for interactive latency workloads.
26:05 Liam: do you have a sample load test harness?
26:10 Samir: yes there's a loader tool under tools/loadtester, it's node-based and can simulate concurrent clients and different prompt sizes. we'll include a readme for running it.
26:30 Priya: last security question — data in transit to Redwood hosted is TLS, keys not stored plaintext; but we need to know retention windows for logs.
26:42 Jordan: default retention 30 days for usage logs, can be configured for enterprise customers; audit logs exportable on demand. we'll share the retention and export steps.
26:55 Maya: awesome. ok final recap?
27:05 Jordan: recap: Jordan to send quickstart repos + cost spreadsheet + security docs; Samir to run perf baseline; Priya to share KMS requirements; schedule POC kickoff w/infra. we'll aim for week of 11/9.
27:20 Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
27:25 (meeting ends)
